title: Early Voting Opens in Texas, Florida as Indian-American Candidates Contest Key Seats
excerpt: Pooja Sethi could become the first Indian American in the Texas Legislature, Pia Dandiya's Florida congressional race is rated a Toss-up, and early ballots are being cast ahead of the November 3 midterms.
body:
• Early voting opened on Monday, October 19, in Texas and in Florida's Palm Beach County, ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, with Indian-American candidates contesting state and congressional seats in both states.
  • In Texas House District 47, Democrat Pooja Sethi would become the first Hindu and the first Indian American in the state Legislature if she wins; in Florida's 22nd Congressional District, Democrat Pia Dandiya's race is rated a Toss-up.
  • Outside groups have spent about $3.8 million against Dandiya and about $7.6 million against Democrat Amish Shah in Arizona, and the super PACs behind much of that spending file their first donor reports on October 20.
  • For voters: Texas early voting runs October 19-30 and registration and polling details are at VoteTexas.gov; Palm Beach County early voting runs October 19 to November 1, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., with a vote-by-mail request deadline of 5 p.m. on October 22.

Voters in Texas and Florida's Palm Beach County began casting early ballots on Monday in midterm races where Indian-American candidates are fighting for state legislative and congressional seats ahead of the November 3 elections, according to IANS reporting published by hi INDiA. The contests are among several across the country — in Arizona, Ohio, New York and California as well — in which Indian-American candidates face competitive races and heavy outside spending.

The Texas Races

In Texas House District 47, Democrat Pooja Sethi is seeking a seat that would make her the first Hindu and the first Indian American elected to the Texas state Legislature. The bar is higher in House District 66, where Democrat Sandeep Srivastava faces Republican Matt Shaheen, who chairs the House Elections Committee and won 61.1 per cent of the vote in 2024. Srivastava lost a 2024 congressional race to Republican Keith Self by 62.5 per cent to 37.5 per cent, IANS reported.

Early voting in Texas runs from October 19 through October 30, with Election Day on November 3, the Texas Secretary of State said. The registration deadline was October 5, and voters can check their status at VoteTexas.gov.

A Dead Heat in Florida

In Florida's 22nd Congressional District, Democrat Pia Dandiya's race against Republican Casey Askar is close to a dead heat. The Cook Political Report and Sabato's Crystal Ball rate it a Toss-up, while Inside Elections rates it Tilt Republican. The forecasting models split in opposite directions: PollingForecast gives Dandiya a 56 per cent chance of winning, and Call the Map gives Askar 54 per cent.

Palm Beach County runs early voting through November 1 at 28 sites, according to the county elections office cited by IANS. The county's own 2026 general election page lists early voting hours of 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. from October 19 through November 1, and says vote-by-mail ballots must be received by 7 p.m. at its main office on Election Day.

Money has moved into the race early. Federal filings show No Going Back PAC has spent about $3.8 million against Dandiya, while groups backing her, including Progressive Turnout Project, LCV Victory Fund and House Majority PAC, have spent more than $560,000, according to IANS.

Battlegrounds Beyond Texas and Florida

In Arizona's 1st Congressional District, Inside Elections on October 15 moved Democrat Amish Shah's race against Republican Jay Feely from Toss-up to Tilt Democrat. Cook rates the race Lean Democrat and Sabato's Crystal Ball rates it a Toss-up. About $7.6 million has been spent against Shah, led by Safety & Affordability PAC's $3.76 million.

The two super PACs targeting Shah and Dandiya have yet to reveal their donors. Both switched to monthly filing in September, and their first reports, covering donors through September 30, are due on October 20, IANS reported.

In Ohio, where early voting is already under way, Democrat Amy Acton has refused to debate Republican Vivek Ramaswamy in the governor's race. "I absolutely will never stand on a stage with someone who has lied in the egregious ways he has, who has a chronic history of lying," Acton told The Vindicator. Ramaswamy told the newspaper he "was shocked" when he learned she would not debate.

New York early voting begins October 24, where Republican Saritha Komatireddy is challenging Attorney General Letitia James. A campaign-commissioned OnMessage poll reported by the New York Post put James ahead 50.7 to 44.7; Siena's September poll had her up 52-39. Los Angeles County vote centers also open October 24, where councillor Nithya Raman is challenging Mayor Karen Bass.

What Happens Next

The next test is turnout during early voting, followed by the October 20 donor disclosures, which will show who financed the super PAC spending against Dandiya and Shah. Election Day is November 3.
